title: Jewelry worth millions of dollars stolen from French museum in daring early-morning raid
facts: Burglars broke into the Lalique museum in Wingen-sur-Moder, France, around 5:30 am on a Sunday. [cite: 250]
Thieves smashed open six display cases inside the Lalique museum's jewelry room. [cite: 250]
Approximately 20 pieces of jewelry were stolen from the Lalique museum during the burglary. [cite: 250]
The estimated value of the stolen Lalique museum jewelry is close to four million euros. [cite: 250]
The jewelry stolen from the Lalique museum was made of crystal without precious gems. [cite: 250]
A cleaning lady was the first person to arrive at the Lalique museum after the burglary and called the police. [cite: 250]
The Lalique museum, dedicated to jeweler and glassmaker Rene Lalique, opened in 2011. [cite: 250]
The Lalique museum houses more than 650 works of Art Nouveau jewelry, Art Deco glass, and contemporary crystal. [cite: 250]
The town of Wingen-sur-Moder has a population of approximately 1,500 inhabitants. [cite: 250]
Thieves stole $102 million worth of jewelry from the Louvre museum in Paris in October 2025. [cite: 250]
A security audit determined that 35% of the rooms in the Louvre's Denon Wing were not monitored by security cameras during the 2025 heist. [cite: 250]
A woman was arrested and charged in October 2025 for stealing gold from the Natural History Museum in Paris. [cite: 250]
Thieves stole three porcelain works from the Adrien Dubouche National Museum in Limoges in September 2025. [cite: 250]
Four men smashed display cases at the Cognacq-Jay museum in Paris in November 2024 to steal 18th-century works. [cite: 250]
The 2024 Cognacq-Jay museum heist resulted in a $4 million insurance payment to the Royal Collection Trust. [cite: 250]
